title: GitLab CI: Switch the Windows builds to Visual Studio 2026
description:
Switch the merge request and package builds to Visual Studio 2026.

AI-Assisted: no
(cherry picked from commit c23d7c2e727aacb620e6e1e969fdf5bcbe46b4e0)

Conflicts:
	.gitlab-ci.yml

notes.body: enabled automatic add to merge train when checks pass

added 4 commits
  • c89e9b58 - GitLab CI: Switch the Windows builds to Visual Studio 2026
  • aa298dd0 - CMake: Let CMake figure out our toolset version
  • 88efd724 - CMake: WiX: Set merge module location correctly
  • afa470d2 - packaging: WiX: Fix toolset version in one more place
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25062/diffs?diff_id=1815402937&start_sha=52f3ff7df3291bf338da3aa1d1b540293c00a8fb)
reset approvals from @johnthacker by pushing to the branch

https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/vcpkg-VTK-build-fails-with-MSVC-1451-af/11090069 

Looks like it is not possible to compile with Qt 6.5.3 with MSVC 2026.

We might be able to update to a 6.6.x or 6.7.x version, which both appears to have fixed it at least in some Qt modules. (https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-118993), and also supports the same macOS and Windows versions as 6.5.x - 6.8.x does not support Windows Server 2016/Windows 10 1607.

(https://github.com/qt/qtbase/commit/6848969cbc7b9a282e9cc22670721e6ed464b29e is the offending commit in Qt 6.8.0 that breaks Windows Server 2016/Windows 10 1607.)
